title: Speaker calls on ASEAN lawmakers to pass laws to increase trade among members, address AI dangers
summary: Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III on Wednesday called on Southeast Asian lawmakers to pass laws which will increase trade and other avenues of cooperation in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations…

blocks.text: Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III on Wednesday called on Southeast Asian lawmakers to pass laws which will increase trade and other avenues of cooperation in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), saying goods should freely flow in the 11-strong regional bloc.
Dy made the call during his keynote speech during the opening of the 47th General Assembly of the ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly.

“Prosperity for all is the very purpose of ASEAN. And parliaments hold the tools to deliver it: laws that open markets fairly, budgets that build roads, ports, and schools, and oversight that ensures the benefits reach those who need them most,” Dy said.

“Growth should widen the circle. A rice farmer should receive a fair price for her harvest. A fisherman should be able to sell his catch in other towns. A small business in a provincial market should be able to reach customers in ten other countries. And a young graduate should be able to find work that makes full use of her talent,” Dy added.
Likewise, Dy said ASEAN lawmakers should stand together in fighting the challenges of artificial intelligence (AI) and regulating its benefits.

“Our farmers are already experiencing the digital transformation. Today, a farmer in the Mekong Delta checks the weather and the price of rice on her phone before deciding when to harvest. A young developer in Laos writes code for a company in Malaysia. A weaver in the Philippines sells her fabric to buyers in Indonesia. This is the ASEAN of 2045 arriving ahead of time. But the same networks also carry scams, disinformation, and threats to our privacy,” Dy said.

“Artificial intelligence is advancing faster than many of our laws can keep pace with. No single parliament can manage these challenges alone. Our parliaments must therefore learn from one another and move forward together: on cybersecurity, consumer protection, the responsible use of AI, and extending connectivity to the last village still waiting for it,” Dy added.

Ultimately, Dy said working together shared prosperity is anchored on the ASEAN’s Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia inked 50 years ago, a commitment that is much needed today as the ASEAN countries bear the brunt of high oil prices amid the war between the United States and Iran.

“Their promise was simple and brave: we will respect one another, we will settle our differences peacefully, and we will work together. Half a century later, that promise still holds. That commitment matters more than ever,” Dy said.

“This year, conflict far from our shores led to higher fuel prices, and families in every one of our countries felt the impact. Through every challenge, the spirit of the Treaty has been our anchor. As parliamentarians, we are the guardians. We keep it alive every time we pick up the phone to reach a counterpart across the border, every time we disagree in this hall and yet part as friends,” Dy added. —VAL, GMA News
